comment: The xTalk Suite extensions that OXT-Beyond ships built in, consumed from
the member repositories at pinned commits (nothing of them is kept in this
repository). tools/oxt/xtalk_extensions.py reads this file: 'pin' resolves
a member's commit and rewrites its commit, version and every file's
sha256, size and (Windows libraries) imports; 'fetch' downloads the files
from raw.githubusercontent.com/<repository>/<commit>/<path> into a cache
and verifies them; 'build' compiles the LCB libraries with lc-compile and
assembles one folder per extension, which tools/oxt/package.py installs
under Extensions/. sha256 and size are those of the git blob (LF line
endings), never of a CRLF working copy. See tools/oxt/README.md.
The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs that build copies next to the
Windows libraries importing them (enetxt, Box2Dxt), pinned by SHA-256 and
size so that a package does not depend on which Visual Studio the
machine that makes it has: build and package.py stop at any other copy
(--allow-unpinned-vc-runtime only warns; never for a release). "redist"
names the redistributable folder they were pinned from (VC\Redist\MSVC\
<version>; 14.44.35112 is Visual Studio 2022 17.14's, the one on the
windows-2022 CI image) and "file_version" their file version.
"xtalk_extensions.py pin-vc-runtime --vc-redist DIR" rewrites "redist",
"file_version" and "files".

members.name: Box2Dxt
members.comment: The version is the module's metadata (0.2.0 at the first pin); the member's CHANGELOG.md already has a [0.3.0] section, so the two disagree upstream. The module id org.openxtalk.box2dxt makes lc-compile warn (a digit in a namespace component), so it is compiled without -Werror.
members.licence: MIT (Seth Morrow and Box2Dxt contributors); the libraries statically link Box2D (MIT); the Windows libraries need the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime
